evidence.excerpt: District heating substations generate continuous telemetry—supply and return temperatures, flow rate, differential pressure, valve position—that reflects both normal load variation and incipient faults. This paper applies isolation forest anomaly scoring to hourly-resampled records from 38 substations in a mid-sized Serbian city, covering two full heating seasons. To reduce the influence of strong daily and weekly periodicity, features were constructed as deviations from a Fourier-smoothed seasonal baseline rather than raw sensor values. Anomaly scores were validated against a maintenance log containing 54 confirmed fault events, yielding precision of 0.69 and recall of 0.78 at the chosen score threshold. False positives were predominantly associated with demand-side events such as building renovations. The paper also discusses operational considerations for deploying the pipeline in the control room of a heat utility, where interpretability requirements constrain model complexity.
